title: This Jellyfish Can Age Backwards and Restart Its Life

scenes.text: There's a jellyfish that ages backwards. It never dies of old age.
It's called the immortal jellyfish, and it's smaller than your little fingernail.
When it's hurt, starving or old, it sinks to the sea floor and melts its adult body into a blob.
That blob becomes a polyp, the baby stage, and buds off brand new jellyfish. A butterfly turning back into a caterpillar.
It works because its cells can switch jobs, a muscle cell turning into a nerve cell, which almost no other animal can do.
In twenty twenty-two, scientists read its genome and found twice as many copies of the genes that repair DNA. Would you restart your life if you could?

description:
There's a jellyfish that can age backwards, and it never has to die of old age.
Turritopsis dohrnii, the immortal jellyfish, is less than 5 mm across. When injured, starving or ageing, it reverts its adult body into a polyp, the juvenile stage, and starts its life cycle again. Its cells can transform into other cell types, a process called transdifferentiation.
A 2022 genome study found it carries twice as many copies of DNA-repair genes as its mortal cousin.
Would you restart your life if you could?
